modv0.1.1

ordersSay it once.

The mod keeps a session's standing orders and puts them back in front of the model after every compaction.

At the prompt of a terminal session:

/plugin install orders --marketplace LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills
Other ways to install

  • From a shell:

    claude plugin install orders --marketplace LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills

  • In the desktop app: click + next to the prompt box, then Plugins, Add marketplace with LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills, then Add plugin.

Read writing-agent-instructions Source on GitHub

Commands

CommandWhat it does
/order use pnpm, never npmkeep a standing order
/orderlist them, each with its number
/order drop 2drop order #2
/order cleardrop them all
/order saytell the model the list again now

In use

When a prompt you type holds "from now on", "from here on", "going forward", "for the rest of this session", "every time you", "each time you", "whenever you" or "don't ever", or has a sentence that starts with "Always" or "Never", a band above the prompt offers to keep that sentence: Keep, or Not this. Your next prompt takes the offer away.

Only a person adds an order. "A person" means the prompt came from the prompt box on your machine or through Remote Control (you, on another device): the same two origins the other mods here trust. An instruction that outlives the turn has to come from you: a web page, a file or a tool result that says "from now on" is something the model read, and it never becomes a standing order. So the mod registers no tool for the model, the band reads only what you typed (never a plugin's, a peer's, a schedule's, a channel's or an SDK host's prompt, and never a slash command), and /order run by anything but you can list or restate the orders and change nothing.

How it behaves

  • Delivery. The model gets the whole list as one hidden message marked [orders], which names the orders as yours and says the list is not a new request. It goes in when an order is added, dropped or cleared, and on /order say, without starting a turn: an idle session's model reads it with your next prompt, a running turn's at its next step. Emptying the list says once that the orders were lifted.
  • Compaction. After a compaction of the main conversation, yours or an automatic one, the list rides once on the next tool result or the next prompt, whichever comes first. A subagent's compaction, a vetoed one and one computed ahead and never installed change nothing. A reply in the gap does not see the list yet: after an automatic compaction, the first answer that calls no tool.
  • /clear starts the conversation over. The orders stay, and ride on your next prompt.
  • Limits. At most 12 orders of at most 500 characters. A repeat of one already kept, ignoring case and spacing, is refused, and the band does not offer it. The status line shows how many orders there are.
  • The orders last as long as the session. They are also kept in the mod's store under the session's id for 30 days, so a session resumed under the same id gets them back. The 30 days count from the last change to the list, not from the last time the session was used.
  • An order is words the model reads, nothing more: the mod does not check that it is followed.
  • The band draws on the terminal and in the desktop app, the two that draw a band above the prompt. Other harnesses ignore this mod.
